utterances.text: Again, between September 1992 and August 1994, what was the reason, if any, for you being in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: To cover the conflict as a photojournalist working on assignment for the Associated Press.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the context of your employment, did you from time to time make observations and speak to individuals on the Bosnian Serb side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there a particular protocol that you observed when you wished to undertake such activities?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: On most occasions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did that protocol involve initially seeing someone at Pale?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Normally, you would need some sort of clearance from the press centre at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that known as the Pale Press Agency?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes, it would -- it might have been. I'm not a hundred percent sure of the actual name.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As it happened, was the person in charge of such matters at that centre or agency the daughter of Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thereafter, if the nature of your contact with the Bosnian Serb side was military in nature, did you go from Pale to the Lukavica barracks?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: On most occasions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If it involved something of a political nature, did you go somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Probably to Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll ask you some questions about the contact of a military nature. What would happen when you arrived at Lukavica barracks?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: You would normally be taken for a briefing, sometimes referred to as a "press conference," depending on the number of journalists present. But it would usually be in the form of a briefing, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: After the briefing, would you thereafter travel to various positions on the Bosnian Serb side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Sometimes. Yeah, most of the times we would do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you did that, were you accompanied by any Bosnian Serb army officials?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Usually officers. Well, a fairly large group, I would say. Several vehicles, perhaps a dozen people altogether, including security. But there would be officers and other military personnel present.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say "officers," do you mean military officers, that is, ranking officers?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Of what army?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Of what we referred to then as the Bosnian Serb army, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On how many occasions during the conflict, first of all - and by that, I refer to the dates of April 1992 until the end of 1995 - did you travel around the Bosnian Serb side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It would have to be an estimate of about a dozen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On how many occasions did you undertake such trips, approximately, between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Eight, ten, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During those visits, did you make any observations of artillery?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Well, we would see artillery positions, usually from afar. We would be taken to positions where we believed there to be artillery that we had requested to go to. Usually you would find an artillery position without a piece of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where did your information come from typically which led you to request that you were taken to a particular site with the expectation of seeing artillery?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: One of the best sources of information would be the UN -- United Nations Military Observers' radio frequency, which was open for anyone to listen to, and they actually gave rough map references as to where outgoing and incoming fire was occurring.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you went to such sites and discovered there wasn't artillery present, did you observe any signs that in the recent past there had been artillery present?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Frequently, you would observe tracks. You would find empty shell casings, obviously sandbagged positions, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to, in a general sense, being on the Bosnian Serb side of the confrontation line, in particular at high elevations over Sarajevo, what observations, if any, did you make as to the clarity of the view of the city, that is, on the other side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Depending on weather, the view of the city would be amazingly clear. You could easily find streets, buildings, and on a good day you might even recognise vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever have any conversations between September 1992 and August 1994 with members of the Bosnian Serb army in relation to the use of artillery?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you ever given an explanation as to the purposes that the artillery was used for?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: They would normally be referred to purely defensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On any occasions between those dates of September 1992 and August 1994, were you ever offered an opportunity to make some use of artillery in those positions, that is, on the Bosnian Serb army side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Well, on the rare occasions where there would actually be an artillery piece in the position, usually a smaller calibre mortar, for instance, yes, we'd be offered to fire the weapon, jokingly perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you take us to any particular example that comes to mind of that happening?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Trebevic, I think in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the nature of the artillery on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I think that was a 105 millimetre howitzer, a towed howitzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What direction was the howitzer pointing when you had the relevant conversation?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Well, it was pointing at the city centre. It's hard to tell because of the elevation, obviously, what the actual aim is, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who was it that made the offer to you?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: On that occasion, I think it was an officer. Yes. It was an officer who seemed to be in charge of this particular artillery position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't expect you to recollect his exact words, but can you give us some sense of what it was that you were told he said?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Well, I think I was offered to pull the lanyard on this weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the lanyard?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: The lanyard is a piece of rope that is attached to the trigger, if you will, on an artillery piece. That's what actually -- there isn't -- you know, on this piece of -- this type of weapon there isn't an actual metal trigger. You use a rope to fire it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In what language was he speaking?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Probably German. I would guess German. I'm not a hundred per cent sure about the language situation. There could be somebody there translating. I wouldn't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And what was your response, if any?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I declined, yes. And then I also -- and this was sort of standard reply, obviously for professional reasons, from our point of view, is to ask, "What would we hit if we fired the weapon?"

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ask that standard question on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I'm reasonably sure that I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recollect the answer?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: The answer was standard or very typical answer, which is they would refer -- they would say, "Turks."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: "Turks"?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: "Turks," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was your understanding, if any, what was meant by the use of the word "Turks"?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Well, one would assume that they were referring to Bosnian Muslims, Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you have any sense of what would have happened if you had in fact pulled the lanyard?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: That was never really an option.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mean in your mind or do you mean in relation to whether you would have been permitted to do so?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I obviously don't know if I would have been permitted to do so. It certainly wasn't an option, from my point of view. It's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you ever made this offer that you've told was made on a number of occasions in relation to small arms or machine-guns or anti-aircraft weaponry or anything of that nature?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes. It's fairly common. That was fairly common, especially small arms weaponry. It could happen during these formal -- well, formal, but yeah, these formal visits that were organised or just passing checkpoints on the way going in and out through Serb lines or trying to go in and out through Serb lines, and you might be on some checkpoint asked if you wanted to fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that for professional reasons you asked a standard question to the effect, "What would I hit if I do so?" or something of that order; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And what were the range of answers that you typically received to that question, if indeed there was a range?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Anything from the -- I don't remember exactly -- the exact word in the local language, but there was a reference to "Turks." There would be "terrorists," there would be -- what else? Yeah. Not very accurate terms. I mean, you never -- very rarely was the other side referred to as -- as the Bosnian government army or anything like that. It was usually referred to as some sort of -- yeah. There was an emphasis on the Muslim, you know, angle on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you ever taken to what appeared to be sniper positions?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On how many occasions, approximately, between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Depending a little bit on how you define "sniper position." A sniper position can be a man with a gun, obviously, who's hiding and firing at -- or wanting to fire at somebody. But I'd say, you know, a more organised sniping position just a few times. I mean, less than five times. It's rough, I'm sorry. I can't give you an exact estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's all right. On these occasions, having regard to your earlier evidence, were you accompanied by an officer of the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Not necessarily. The -- there is an emphasis on discretion when you move into a sniper position, and you very often go -- very often, but you would go alone with somebody taking you up into the position, or indeed the sniper, as it were, himself would take you to show you his quarters, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the occasions or occasion that a sniper would take you himself to show you his quarters, where would you make contact with the sniper in the first place?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Usually as part of a visit to, you know, the area that the position was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say a "part of a visit," you mean part of a visit with an officer?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes, definitely. There was no way you could move around on Bosnian Serb -- what we referred to then as the Bosnian Serb army-held territory without an escort. We were -- I don't recall hearing of journalists ever moving around. I'm sure someone has at some point been able to do this, but I've never heard of a foreign journalist ever travelling around Bosnian Serb areas without an official escort and without having gone through the proper procedure or a procedure in advance of that. And there would be officers present during these trips, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And an officer who would join you at Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: For instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Any other places?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Well, there was a Serb -- Bosnian Serb army liaison officer in Sarajevo airport for a large part of the war. I don't recall if we would go directly from there or then via Lukavica and/or Pale or Ilidza or whatever, but I think visits could be arranged through him. But these procedures changed all the time. There was always a new piece of paper that had to be signed or a new, you know, fax number that you had to send a fax to. I mean, all -- you know, it's a fairly bureaucratic approach, and it was fairly -- I mean, very often declined. It was very rare that you would actually get, you know, a permission to visit, you know, on your first attempt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Just in relation to your evidence that you were taken to sniper positions or did go to sniper positions on the Bosnian Serb army side, did you ever go to any high-rise positions, that is, sniper positions in high-rise buildings?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I went to building in -- buildings in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: That would have been the winter of 1993. Either late 1993 or early 1994. It wasn't actually possible to go there. I mean, 1992, 1993, it would have been deemed too dangerous because the fighting was so intense. And I think only in late 1993 was it -- did it actually become possible to go to Grbavica without taking a tremendous risk.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you mentioned "buildings." That is plural. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: There were, as far as I recall - well, I think they are still there - a number of high-rises in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And what was the proximity of these buildings to each other, that is, the high-rise buildings?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: They were pretty close together. I think in a line maybe, oh, 50 to 100 metres apart, something like that, no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many in the line?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it's exactly in a line, but lined up sort of. Four perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What, approximately, were the number of storeys? Well, first of all -- I'll withdraw that. Did each of the four or so high-rise buildings appear to have the same number of floors? In other words, were they about the same height?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did they appear to be part of the same development? In other words, did they have similar appearances, one to each of the others?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes. It has to be pointed out here that these were the sort of buildings you normally would not want to see very clearly, for obvious Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. reasons, when you were on the Bosnian government side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And approximately how many storeys were they?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Oh, at least 10 or 12, possibly more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to your second to last answer, do you mean that they had a certain reputation or do you mean something else?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: You were -- and I was frequently fired at myself, going past those buildings because it was, especially in -- well, throughout 1992 and 1993, before there was any effective anti-sniper measures from the UN or any other party, they basically controlled a large chunk of the road that you had to travel to get to the western part of the city. So it was a case of picking up as much speed as you could in your car and going past there as fast as you possibly could.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And on what side of the confrontation line do you mean in terms of where you were at the time that this happened --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- that you would be shot at?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I would on the Bosnian government side, going past these buildings heading east or west past them. And it was a fairly reliable thing. I mean, you could -- I remember on one occasion actually making a bet inside an armoured vehicle as to whether the same sniper would hit the car coming back as they did when we went past it going out. And indeed, the sniper did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In your mind, were you left with any doubt as to the source of the fire?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: If you add up the reports from UNMO's observation that you could make at a greater distance where you could -- in the beginning, the snipers were not very professional. Actually, you could see dust, smoke, even muzzle flashes partially because there was no one to engage them. They were basically at liberty to operate in a fairly relaxed manner and so on. Yes, it was pretty easy to figure out where it was coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So at a later point, you found yourself inside one of those same buildings?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: A fairly basic sniper position, not a very sophisticated one, heavily sandbagged, also probably with pieces of, you know, concrete blocks, things that had been removed from walls, used as well as cover. And then various types of weaponry, nothing extremely sophisticated. And a few people who obviously sort of, you know, occupied this house or -- it's basically a combination of two rooms usually that creates a sniper position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You've said that this was late 1993 or early 1994. Whenever it was precisely, after that visit, did you at any time have the same experience of being shot at when driving past those buildings?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Oh, yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On this occasion that you were taken there, was there a Bosnian Serb army officer with you?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: On the -- outside the building, definitely, there would have had to have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In terms of accompanying you on your visit.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes. But if he actually came with me into the building, I wouldn't know. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Had he taken you to the buildings?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes. There was no way we would have been able to go on our own. In Grbavica, highly contested area, close to the line of confrontation, you're exposed -- you're very much exposed when you travel there, and there's no way we would have been allowed to go on our own anywhere near those buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On that occasion, were you taken there pursuant to a request from you or their initiative or what?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I honestly don't remember. It might have been as a result of a request because this was one of the -- it's a very -- because of the extent of the sniping that was going on, it was a very important part of the story. So we always tried to get as much information about it as possible. So it might have been after repeated requests, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, in relation to the position of these apartment blocks, I think you've told us they were approximately in a line, and there were about four, 10 or 12 storeys high. Can you think of any landmarks that were nearby so we can establish the position?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Let me see. Unfortunately, being a photographer doesn't mean that you have a photographic memory. There is a stadium in that area I think called Grbavica stadium, which is I think behind -- to the south of those buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mean immediately to the south, or to the south and to the west or to the south and to the east? Or if you're not sure, please say so.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I couldn't, you know...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. In relation to Grbavica, were there any other high-rise apartment blocks nearby other than these four, or was there something reasonably unique about them?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Not in the immediate area, no, as far as I remember. Just add to that, when you're actually inside a position like that, inside a building like that that is so close to the front line, you don't have much of a view. I mean, you basically see the small area that is targeted by the sniper. All the other buildings -- in an area like that, in a building like that, that close to the confrontation line, you don't go past open windows that allow you a view. So it's fairly disorientating when you're inside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you said earlier that you drive past the buildings many times with some degree of apprehension as to what would happen to you. And on numerous occasions, you, in fact, received rounds that came from those buildings. So from that perspective, from the other side of the confrontation line, approximately where were these four buildings?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: They were -- well, obviously to the south of the main road, going -- you'd have the -- it wasn't far -- you would have the Marsal Tito barracks more or less on your right when you went past there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that when you're heading west or east?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: When you're heading west.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So at the time that the apartment buildings were on your left, you would have Marsal Tito somewhere to your right. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes, roughly. I mean, I can't remember exactly the relation, but it's in that general area, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, whilst you were in one of those buildings, did you observe any weaponry?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you observe?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I think on that occasion, I saw an M-84, general purpose machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was that known by another name, locally and colloquially?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes. I think I'm not going to attempt the local --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Translation, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: But the translation, something like the death sower or death spreader. We got different versions of that. But I'm not going to attempt the local name because I can't remember exactly what it's like. It's a -- how shall I say? It's based on the Kalashnikov design, somewhat larger, fires from a belt. In this case, would have been fitted with a scope and was probably -- it was on a bipod rather than on a larger tripod or mount.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the sound that the death sower made?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It's fairly characteristic, fairly sharp. It depends on whether you're on the receiving end or the other end. But being fired at by it is a very frightening experience. It makes a very loud noise. The sound of the rounds going past you is very loud. They have fairly high velocity. It's quite confusing because there is what we call a high-velocity snap as the round goes by, and that occurs before you hear the sound of the gun firing. So it can be quite confusing, yeah. When they're actually firing it, or if you're near it being fired, it's so deafening that you don't really -- it's a lot louder than a Kalashnikov, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You used the word, I think, "characteristic" -- excuse me a moment. Your words were, "It's fairly characteristic, fairly sharp."

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to those words, did you feel that you could distinguish when a death sower was being fired as opposed to another machine-gun or another type of weapon?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Depending on distance, you know, terrain, buildings, there's all kinds of factors. But if you have, you know, an AK-47 fired from the same position as an M-84, you'll be able to tell the difference -- most people would be able to tell the difference. The M-84 has a slightly higher rate of fire if it's fired on full automatic. And the sound of the incoming rounds is, you know, a lot more. You know, the AK-47 fires a fairly slow round which you don't hear that well when it comes in, unless it impacts on something.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, amongst your photojournalism activities, in recent years, have you set up a consultancy specialising in hostile environment training and operational support?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does that involve you and others, including military experts, providing training to other journalists, nongovernment organisation representatives, on how to survive in a hostile environment and in a combat situation?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you consider that you have any particular expertise in this area?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Certainly have a lot of experience, and real experience, not just from training. I mean, I've covered something like a dozen, or worked in something like a dozen war zones. I've made a lot of mistakes and learned from them, hopefully. I'm still here. I try to keep myself up to date on what happens in, you know, various conflicts and in the world of military operations. And I study cases of journalists being hurt or killed very thoroughly in order to find out if there's anything that can be learned from those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Incidentally, in that regard, given the large number of previous conflict situations you attended, did you notice anything different in Sarajevo, that is, casualties amongst journalists?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I think there was a perception, and I think an accurate perception, amongst most of us who had experience from previous conflicts that this was the first conflict in which media personnel -- recognisable media personnel were actively targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say "recognisable," did you have a vehicle between September 1992 and August 1994 whilst you were in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: We had several, but the Associated Press -- I brought the Associated Press's first armoured vehicle into Sarajevo in September of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What type of vehicle was it? Not what brand; was it a truck or a sedan or something else?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It's a -- well, it can easily be described as a pickup version of a Land Rover.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What colour was it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It was white.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you place any markings on it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It had bright orange fluorescent tape markings all over it, basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did they depict any characters or numbers or anything?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: We used -- it's very hard to tape the words "Press"; it takes a long time. So we used the words "TV" instead. And basically, the entire sides of the vehicle, bonnet, roof, back of the car, would be covered with the word "TV".

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So the four sides and the roof?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You notice -- first of all, before you placed the tape on the vehicle, did it ever come under fire?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Well, the car was marked when we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Had you had vehicles before that one arrived?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Oh, yes, definitely; soft-skinned, normal -- regular rental cars, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In any event, you received that one in September 1992. Did the vehicle ever receive any fire?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With what degree of -- on more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: On -- it was basically -- I think it's still in existence today, and it looks like a Swiss cheese basically live. It has holes, impacts. Part of the car is not armoured. It's only the cab, you know, where the passengers sit that is armoured. So the engine room and the back of the pickup is soft skin aluminium, and that is more or less perforated by incoming fire, shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could go to an example in relation to this. Was there an incident which occurred in the fall of 1994 where the vehicle was shot at involving a --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I'm sure there were many.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Involving a water point in the form of a well?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: We took the -- yes. We went to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before you go into the detail --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- did you start that experience with you being at Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And was there a reason why you were at Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: We probably went to Kosevo hospital because we heard either the arrival of ambulances or we heard firing, you know, more than the usual amount of firing somewhere. It's a fairly routine -- it was a fairly routine, you know, thing to visit the hospitals several times a day to keep tabs on what was going and certainly where it was going on, because you go there, you'd actually find out where the casualties had come from and then be able to assess whether or if it was worthwhile going there in order to find out what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that what happened this time?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It was indeed, yes. There was casualty there who had been taken from this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you describe the casualty that arrived at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I think it was a man who had been hit in the abdomen, as far as I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What sort of clothing was, if any, he wearing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't be able to recall exact details of his clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: He might have been -- no. I mean, there was -- I think he was a fairly young man. I'm not a hundred -- I think he was a fairly young man. He was probably wearing blue jeans and sneakers and a T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly request that counsel make pauses between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hvaal, I would also like to draw to your attention that the interpretation may have some difficulties since you are in a very quick conversation with the -- with counsel for the Prosecution. So would you please look at your screen and wait until it stops moving before you're answering the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly. Certainly. I wasn't aware of that. I'll keep an eye on it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you go to where you understood he had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: We did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you see when you arrive at that position?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: We saw -- well, we went to a -- I think a well in the location in Sedrenik which was -- there's a well just by the road, on the lower side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you see any people?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes. There were people there hiding. I think -- yeah. There was a building or some sort of structure there, and I think there were people hiding there and down in the actual well because there was fire coming from the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts on the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It was within -- you could see a known Bosnian Serb army position called -- that was referred to -- by us as Sharp Stone feature because we couldn't pronounce the local name. And I would estimate that to be 300 to 400 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the topography of Sharp Stone?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Sharp Stone is what it sounds like. It's a cliff-like formation basically, and it usually had a flag on top of it, or often had a flag on top of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Being a cliff, I take it there was the ground above the cliff and the ground below?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts was the front line in relation to the cliff?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Below the cliff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How far from the base of the cliff? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Not very far, but that was a very -- it was a dodgy area that because of the topography being -- it was very steep in that area, and you didn't actually have sort of a trench or a marked front line. This is to my recollection, but as far as I remember, it was a matter of firing positions, well-dug-in firing positions rather than an actual sort of manned front line, as it were, because it would be impossible to keep any kind of personnel in the -- you know, below that point itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Having regard to your evidence so far, do I take it that the cliff top was 300 to 400 metres away from where you were?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And fire was coming from the cliff top?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you -- withdraw that. Whereabouts was the fire arriving?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: The fire was -- oh, when we arrived -- we heard shots when we arrived. People were hiding. We then drove -- or we waited. I can't remember if we went past it and then waited in a better position where we wouldn't be so exposed or if we stopped before we became exposed and waited, but I think we waited for a few minutes to see, you know, what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. If I could just stop you there. You've told us about the group of people.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were any of them wearing any military-type clothes?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were they one sex or both sexes?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Both sexes. I assume -- they'd probably be mostly female.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether any of them appeared particularly elderly or particularly young?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I don't think there were any children as such there, but older people, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do they appear to have been engaged in an activity?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: They were collecting water.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So did you at some point bring your vehicle to a position close to them?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: We decided to investigate what had happened and also to try to get some photographs, and in order to achieve that, I decided to park the vehicle or stop the vehicle in the position that would shield the water point from this incoming fire as much as possible. This was an armoured vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did something happen shortly after you did that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Well, my interpreter got out of the car first, and as I was getting out, a round impacted in the windshield of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the nature of the glass in the windshield?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It was bulletproof or armoured.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the round penetrate the windshield?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It did not, thankfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice something about the force of the round?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It was powerful enough to make the car, which weighs several Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. thousands kilos, rock on its suspension.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts were you in relation to the impact point on the windscreen at the time the bullet hit? And would you please wait a moment before you answer.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I was inside the vehicle, on my way out. I was probably -- well, my head would have been fairly close to the impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, was this the vehicle with the TV markings?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It was indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said you used bright orange; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Bright orange, sort of what the Americans refer to as DayGlo tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you persevere with driving a marked press vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: For some time. It was a matter of principle, obviously, but eventually we gave up on that and attempted to sort of -- sort of adopt a more generic large, white nondescript vehicle that could be a NGO, a UN, an embassy, anything like that to sort of create a little bit more doubt as to what the exact nature of our business was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Right. And finally in relation to this incident, you've said it was, or you've agreed it was in the fall of 1994. Can you be more precise as to when this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It would have been early in the fall because it was still -- the weather was still warm.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, do you wish me to continue? I note the time. I'm happy to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If this would be a suitable moment for you for a break -- I should have indicated that earlier, I think. It's half past twelve. So if this would be a suitable moment, we will then adjourn until ten minutes to one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us that you were the recipient on numerous occasions throughout that period, from September 1992 to August 1994, of small-arms fire. Did you make any observations as to whether civilians, that is, people who appeared to be civilians, were targeted in the same period, apart from the incident that you've just told us about?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With what degree of frequency? How commonplace was it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: You mean people being targeted or actually being hit?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Being targeted.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Being targeted, more or less every day, if not every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean by that that you observed that more or less every day, if not every day?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: If you moved around in downtown Sarajevo in that period, and as a photographer, most of your work consisted of driving around or walking around looking for, you know, whatever was going on, you would observe people being fired at with small arms. I would say every day you go out, you would observe that at some point, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you come to any conclusion or form any opinion as to whether civilians were deliberately targeted or not during that period?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I would say they definitely were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that you observed such things virtually on a daily basis. How often were they successfully targeted? In other words, how often, on your observations during that same period, were civilians actually hit by small-arms fire deliberately?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: You mean that I was personally there to see?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Firstly, that you were there personally to see.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to give you a number, but it's... Depends on how accurate -- I mean, if I actually have to see the impact, or if I arrive a half a minute later or -- it's very difficult to get --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In rough figures, firstly, seeing the impact.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Seeing the impact of people actually being fired at, or hit, I must have seen that on - I don't know - several dozen occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Several dozen.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yeah. I wouldn't be able to give you an exact answer on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I appreciate that. But again, approximately, what would be the number where you either saw them hit or arrived within minutes of them being hit, in that same period?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: "Within minutes," you mean up to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Say half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Up to say half an hour. Oh, 50 to a hundred times probably. I mean, one of the most essential parts of our work was to try and, you know, get an idea of what the sniping situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, would it sometimes happen that you would simply come across such incidents?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there an incident which occurred -- withdraw that. Was there such an incident which occurred in the winter of 1993, that is, towards the end of 1993 or the beginning of 1994, when you were driving along Marsal Tito Boulevard and you saw a woman who had been hit?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Could have happened -- I mean, that would have happened on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Let me be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness be shown a bundle of photographs which are marked P3625. I have copies for my friends and for Your Honours. I think they have already been distributed. It is a bundle of five photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please go through the five photographs, and you see one which shows -- appears to show two men lifting a woman by her arms either on to or off a stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Would you please place that photograph on the overhead viewer. Did you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I did indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember when it was you took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It would have been in the winter of 1993, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were you when you took it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: This is outside the morgue at the Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you tell us the story that goes with that photograph, sir.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: This is -- I came across this woman. I was driving in an armoured Land Rover, heading east, I believe. I'm not a hundred percent sure, but probably heading east. When I came to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On what road, if I could interrupt?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: On the Marsal Tito Boulevard, yeah. I came to one -- there's two intersections that were particularly notorious for sniping in that area. It would have been one of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you tell us the names of these two intersections?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I can't remember the names of -- I think one was -- I can't remember the names of the streets now. I'm sorry. It's -- but it's the two streets that form an "A" that go up towards the Olympic stadiums.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say "go up towards," do you mean in a northerly direction?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: In a northerly direction, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It was on one of those intersections, and I came there and this woman had been hit in either her lower abdomen or in one of her legs. She was in the street, still conscious and moving but not really going anywhere. It's very hard to hear inside an armoured vehicle if there are rounds coming in, so you have to assume that there are. I decided that in order to try to facilitate -- there were other pedestrians in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were they doing, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: They were, at this point I think, taking cover or trying to organise some sort of rescue effort. I'm not a hundred per cent sure if they were out in the street yet or if they were sort of shouting to her to try to go into cover, because this is one of many incidents like this. Usually it's a matter of a short time before someone runs out, and this is what you have to try to keep -- you know, prevent people from doing because very often then you have another casualty and then it just escalates into a very difficult situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why would you have another casualty when someone runs out to assist a wounded person?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It's a pattern of the sniping at civilians in Sarajevo that the first victim would be shot in such a way that they would be wounded. Very often also the patient -- you know, victim doesn't die right away, as long as it's not, you know, a direct hit in the head, and the sniper would then wait for people to come out and try to help. Now, obviously the more people who are injured, the slower the rescuing process becomes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. If you can just spell it out. When you say more people would be injured --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- and you say that the sniper would wait, what do you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: There was a pattern of not, to put it crudely, finishing off victims that had been hit but to wait for help to arrive and then fire at people trying to help.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So rather than deliberately shoot to kill the first victim, do you mean deliberately shoot to wound the first victim so as to encourage rescuers to attend the scene and then shoot the rescuers?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I think in the first -- it's probably giving the snipers too much credit to say that they were consciously shooting to wound rather than to kill. It's a fairly difficult craft, so they'd be probably lucky to hit in the first place. But the average -- you know, the normal regular impact from one small-arm bullet is not going to kill instantly unless it hits the victim in the head or in one of the vital organs. So if you aim low, basically, the person will live for some time, even if, you know, he or she is hit in the abdomen. So I'd say there was a pattern of aiming low perhaps and then not firing at, you know, an injured casualty several times, rather to wait for another person or several people to arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And then to shoot at those people?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: And then to fire at them. And this could sometimes turn into a fairly macabre situation where you would have several casualties as a result of this and no effective means of evacuating them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, as you approached this woman who was lying in the road and apparently still alive, was there anything about her appearance which indicated to you her status in terms of being civilian or military?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Well, she was a lady, I'd say, in her -- well, judging in the photograph as well, probably in her 60s, late 50s, early 60s perhaps. She's wearing a fur coat, as far as I remember, or at least, you know -- not very tall, longish hair. Yeah. Make-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And what -- sorry. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: No. She's wearing make-up, and I mean, she's easily identified as a female, elderly female.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you form any view as to her status, as to whether she was civilian or military?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I would assume that she was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So what did you do after you saw her there?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Well, I tried to put the car into a position where it would again provide some sort of cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Cover from where?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Cover from the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was to the south?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: The south you would have -- what is to the south right there? I can't remember the name of the location, but there is a hill. It probably goes up towards -- I can't remember the name of that location, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the significance to you? What was the importance of providing cover --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and the witness please make pauses between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You heard the request from the translation booth to make more pauses between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. What was the reason that you wished to provide her with cover from the south?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Because that would be the direction that the incoming fire was coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What side of the confrontation line would the incoming fire have come from?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: In that area, you had a -- if you stood where she was lying, you could see Bosnian Serb-held territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you form a view as to where the fire had come from in terms of which side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Not -- I mean, in this particular case, I was too busy trying to be of assistance. But there was a -- I mean, this intersection, as, indeed, both of those two intersections that I mentioned, were fired at daily. And the firing came from the same location all the time. It was -- this had been investigated by the UN; it had been investigated by every possible means. And yeah, it was pretty -- we assumed that it was coming from BSA-held territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mean by that that your assumption was based on the investigation results as you understood them?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: And, of course, the sort of ballistic facts, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Such as?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Such as impacts in vehicles when you drive past, the markings on the ground. At this stage, I think there were some freight containers that had been put up in this area. However, they were more or less empty and bullets travelled through them easily. And you could, you know, without too much ballistic knowledge, find out where the bullet was coming from just by looking through the two holes, that is, if you dared.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever do that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Not personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Coming back to this incident, can you tell us what happened as you went to place your vehicle in a way that offered her protection from the south?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Before -- in these situations, there was always a lot of shouting and, you know, people were obviously arguing about what to do. Everyone knew the risks of going into the street. People didn't -- most civilians didn't quite have an understanding of the armoured vehicles in the sense that they would provide reasonably effective cover. So it always took a little while before you could, you know, effectively intervene. But to my recollection, she was hit again before we could actually get her to safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were you when she was hit again?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I think to the west of her.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you still in your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I would have been, yeah, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you actually see that informed you that she had been hit again?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: This one was hit directly, I think, in the back of the head. I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you notice anything by way of blood at the time of impact?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: There was a clearly visible impact in her head.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you actually see?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Blood, brain matter spraying from the impact. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And how far away from her were you, approximately, when she received the hit to the head?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: 10 metres?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Well, we continued the process that we had started. I mean, I then moved the car further forward. As I did that, I think another car -- a local civilian car arrived and basically did -- picked her up and -- yes. She was picked up by the people, I think, in that car that stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: To my left, it would have been, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the car go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It went to Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you follow it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I followed it to provide cover because you're exposed to some of the same positions when you go up that hill. You can actually get fired at from behind a fair distance, going up that hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And whereabouts were you when you took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It's -- this is the entrance to the morgue at Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who were the two men?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: The two men I think are people who... At least one of them works there. I'm not sure about the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you have occasion to go to cemeteries in the same period of time, that is, between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How often would you attend cemeteries in that period?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Several times a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It's -- it was a dramatic photographic visual documentation of the impact that this was having on the population in the city. It was a good way of keeping track of casualties. And unfortunately, it was often a good way of getting a measure of how -- how shall I say? When I arrived in June 1992, I was told that they were -- the Bosnian Serb army were shelling funerals. I went to find out for myself, and it turned out to be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many times, approximately, during that same period of time did you personally witness funeral processions being shelled?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Again, depends on your definition of "shelling."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Shells arriving either amongst a funeral procession, that is, in the midst of a funeral procession, or within a distance of, say, 50 metres?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: 50 metres is probably a bit close. I wouldn't be here if I had experienced many of those. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question. On how many occasions in that period of time did you witness what you believed to be the deliberate targeting of funeral processions or funerals?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: 20 to 30 times, as an estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Would you please go again to the photographs which are Exhibit P3625. And select -- take from them the photograph which appears to show a woman swinging an axe in a cemetery. Could you please place that photograph on the overhead viewer. Did you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: That would be in the winter of 1992, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why did you take the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: For several reasons. It shows with some degree of clarity a large number of fresh graves. If you examine it more closely -- I don't think you can see it on the screen. But if you examine it closely, you'll see all of those graves are marked 1992 or 1993. It shows that there's a funeral going on in the background. And then, probably most importantly, it shows the level of desperation involved for this woman who is cutting down this tree and chopping it into firewood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did something happen shortly after you took this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: A mortar shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Between the woman and the funeral procession or the actual funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And approximately how far did that shell land from the funeral party?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Roughly halfway between the two. That would mean 75 metres, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: After that mortar shell landed, did something else happen of a similar nature?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I think the funeral party dispersed, took cover, or moved off or tried to, and I think -- yes. I'm pretty sure that another round came in, but that would have fallen far or sort of on the other side again, further Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. down the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any apparent reason as to why, if indeed it was targeted, it would have landed there, further down the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Assuming that they were indeed trying to hit the funeral party, this would have been what's known as bracketing, meaning that if you can see that one round falls short, you then try to make the other round further out.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, just to clarify the degree of recollection that you have of this, how many mortar rounds do you actually remember falling during this incident?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: At least two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I don't know how long I sort of stuck around. I mean, it's not -- not the most pleasant, you know -- I do remember that the woman didn't leave. She stayed for the entire thing. She didn't even take cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you say anything to her about that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I urged her to take cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did she say anything in response?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: She swore, I suppose, at the assumed direction from where this was coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mean the direction or the people?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: The people, I suppose. Yes. I mean, she used words that, with my limited knowledge of the language, would indicate that she was not happy with the people who were firing the weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You say that she didn't take cover. What did she do?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: She kept -- she kept on chopping wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: She kept on chopping wood. All right. Now, you've told us that you've observed the shelling of funeral parties on a large number of occasions during that period. Did you ever find yourself in immediate danger on any of those occasions? Perhaps I should say in a greater degree of danger than you were on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes. I think there were times where the shelling came even closer than that, yes, but it's -- this particular cemetery is so-called Lion's Cemetery, and it eventually became impossible to go to during daylight hours, and we avoided it for that reason. But as -- I mean, there are many reasons for that, but, yeah, it was -- covering cemeteries became eventually something that was considered to be very dangerous, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Indeed, did you notice that funerals, after awhile, took place at night rather than --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- rather than in daylight hours?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: By the -- I'd say by the end of 1993, that had become the rule. Only in exceptional cases would funerals be held in daylight.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, will you please go back to the group of photographs, and this time take from the bundle and place on the overhead projector photograph marked last five numbers 5592 [sic]. When did you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: That would have been in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What does it show? In other words, what are the people doing?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: These are people running from sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the background, there appear to be a number of vehicles. One in particular appears to be a pickup-type vehicle with some items on the roof of the cabin. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think it's blue and white, and it's facing you while you take the photograph, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What type of vehicle was that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: That type of vehicle was commonly used as an ambulance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you recollect or can you recognise what make of vehicle it was?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: This one is probably a locally made car, like a Yugo or a Zastava.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You say that -- that the vehicle was an ambulance. What were the objects on the cabin roof?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: They were blue lights or -- yeah, I think blue. I can't remember the colour, but lights.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Typically when the ambulance was carrying patients, would the lights be operating or not?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Usually not, to my recollection. The main way of moving -- the thing is, all vehicles had to serve as ambulances when there was an incident. Whatever vehicle was closest would basically pick up the casualty and take them to hospital, because there was no means of communication so that an ambulance could be called. Now, the reason this one is sitting here is because this is a known area for sniper activity, and they are actually waiting in case there is a casualty that has to be evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During that same period of time, from September 1992 until August 1994, did you ever observe ambulances marked as the one in the photograph to be hit by small-arms fire?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Rarely, occasionally, frequently, or what, in terms of how often that would happen?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It's hard to -- I mean, basically all cars could be fired at at any time when you were in an area that was exposed to incoming fire. Whether or not the vehicle was marked to appear as an ambulance didn't seem to make any difference. I certainly never noticed there being a changed in behaviour when it came to ambulances or nonambulances, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please now place on the overhead projector Photograph 5583. When did you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: In 1993, I believe in August, September -- no, a bit later. The autumn of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were you when you took it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Inside what we referred to as the French hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were the nature of her injuries?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: She had -- at this point, she is in a coma. She has been hit by -- she has multiple trauma from shrapnel -- mortar shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, I think the photo depicts what appears to be a young girl lying on a bed with a doll in the area of her fingers and some tubes leading to her body. Did you make any inquiries as to how she came by her injuries?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you learn?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: That she had been struck by shrapnel from a mortar impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you discover whether there were any other casualties from the impact?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I believe she was with her mother and another woman at the time, and that her mother was killed, possibly also the other woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you discover where they were at the time of the mortar impact?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I think in Novi Sarajevo, but I'm not sure. I can't recall exactly. I wasn't there when the mortar incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Did you learn her name?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Her name was Irma Hadzimuratovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As a result of your photograph, did this instance, this young girl, attract a great deal of international publicity?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It did indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that because you reported that doctors had told you that, without treatment that they could not provide, she would die?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: We were told that she was -- they were unable to do anything other than keep her alive for a short period of time, and that she was also tying up important resources that they could use for cases that could actually be saved. And that there were a number of other children in similar situations. The doctor actually urged us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Simply, Mr. President, I believe that we see a very -- a perfect example of a leading question. And I don't think I heard the witness say, but I can check it, that the doctors -- the doctors had told him that before, before it was suggested to him by the counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I confess to leading. It was deliberate on my part for the reasons I explained earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And ultimately, as my experience transpires, there is no contest --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is an objection to it. Please rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. What were you told, if anything, by her treating doctors as to her prognosis?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: We were invited by her doctor to come and see her in the first place. And we were told that her prognosis under these conditions, with no running water, no electricity, no heating, and very basic medical equipment, was very poor, that she would die within a short period of time. We were also told that there were many children in similar condition in the various hospitals in Sarajevo. And we were urged by the doctor and other members of the hospital staff to report on this situation so that the world's attention might be drawn to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As a result -- withdraw that. Did you do that? In other words, did you report on this particular girl and the circumstances as explained to you by her doctors?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: We did, indeed. We filed a story about her and this, or very similar photograph, I believe, that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As a result of that, was she transported to the United Kingdom for treatment?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: She was evacuated to the United Kingdom, and this started -- this prompted the United Nations to organise a larger evacuation of I think several hundred wounded children from Sarajevo that happened in the days and weeks after this story became sort of a major issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did she survive?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you some questions about Kosevo Hospital. Where were you living in Sarajevo during that same time period, September 1992 to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Either at a hotel or a motel called the Motel Belvedere, which is located in Visnjik Street. And then eventually, from late 1993, I had my own flat further up on Visnjik Street in Number 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How far was the Hotel Belvedere from the nearest point of the Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Say, about a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've told us earlier that a modus operandus that you employed was to attend the hospital when you heard horns or sirens because that often indicated the imminent arrival of casualties. Do you remember giving that evidence?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that something that you could hear from where you resided when you were at the Hotel Belvedere?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes. And we also had our office at the Motel Belvedere, so we were basically there, somebody from the Associated Press was there 24 hours a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you also hear those sounds from where you moved to further up the street?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes, but I was basically only there for a few hours in the middle of the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. As a result of hearing horns and the like from Belvedere Hospital [sic] in particular, did it happen that you often attended the hospital at about the same time that casualties arrived from time to time during that same period?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
