utterances.text: Did you notice -- withdraw that. On any such occasion, did you make any observations as to whether there was any incoming fire apparently in that vicinity?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: There was frequently incoming fire in and around the hospital grounds. It often increased with the level of activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With the level of what sort of activity?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Vehicles arriving and leaving, people being carried on stretchers from building to building. Yeah, that sort of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What sort of fire do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: The hospital would be -- I've personally seen mortars of various sizes landing there, and howitzer rounds. I've even seen 155, 155-millimetre howitzer rounds impacting very near to the hospital, and I think tank rounds as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Have you ever observed casualties, that is, any persons being injured by incoming fire, be it shell-fire or small-arms fire?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Several times. There was one incident, I think, in -- there were several incidents where hospital staff and patients were -- were wounded. There was -- yeah. There were several incidents when that happened. I remember seeing at least one of them arriving just after -- or being there, in fact, when the building was hit and by, I think, a large heavy-calibre howitzer round, and at least some nurses and a doctor or at least hospital staff were killed during that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And to be clearer, were you present when that happened?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: I was present when the round impacted. I didn't actually see the people being hurt because it was a couple of floors up in the building and it wasn't considered safe to go there, so -- but we saw the dead bodies afterwards, if that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: That would have been in -- the winter of 1993, 1994, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever observe or hear what appeared to be outgoing fire from the vicinity of Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: No, not -- it can be hard to determine the -- you know, the location of small-arms fire sometimes, but no heavy calibre weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever observe or hear what appeared to be the firing of mortar rounds from in or in the vicinity of Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: How -- what is "the vicinity" here?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the closest position to Kosevo hospital that you have seen or heard what you believe to be outgoing mortar fire?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: At least a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: You're saying seen or heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Heard what you believed to be --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yeah. Maybe on a dozen occasions, something like that. I wouldn't -- I'm not a hundred per cent sure here that these are -- normally would be mobile units rather than fixed positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you describe to us what a mobile mortar unit was?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: In this case, it would be a mortar in the back of a Volkswagen Golf.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And do you mean fired from the back of the Volkswagen Golf?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: No. You would lift it out, put it on the ground, fire off a few rounds, and put it back in the Golf and leave. Or any vehicle, obviously, but leave, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you develop the ability to determine the approximate size of a mortar by either the sound of it being -- firstly, by the sound of it being fired?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Again depending on circumstances, but, yes, if you had a comparative and if you had been listening to it often. I wouldn't be able to do it now, I don't think, but at the time certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you, firstly, form any view as to whether on these occasions it was always the same size mortar?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever actually observe the mortar being fired in those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there a regular pattern to the behaviour? In other words, did the -- was there a sequence of events which would typically occur?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: It would be at night, and like I said, it -- basically what I described earlier, a vehicle would arrive carrying typically a mortar, fire off a few rounds in, you know, a short period of time and then pack up and leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On these occasions that you made these observations, did you notice whether any of the individuals were wearing any uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Usually.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What type of uniform?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: Depends on when -- when during the conflict it was, but camouflage uniforms. I mean, there was a smattering of different types of uniforms in use.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever see or hear what you presumed to be mortars being fired from within the hospital grounds?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, we're close to a quarter to two. If you would find a good moment to finish for today, please indicate so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One more question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever see or hear what you presumed to be small-arms fire from within Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I might indicate that I expect I will only be approximately another 15 minutes with this witness in chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Another 15 minutes, yes. Thank you very much. We will adjourn and -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you're standing on your feet. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you so much for giving me the floor, Mr. President. This is just to indicate what I have already said, that unfortunately I have an arbitration session tomorrow and Monday, so I will not be able to be at two hearings, and I would like to ask the Chamber to forgive me and to excuse me. It is impossible for me to do otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that you have other obligations as well. There's one other remark I'd like to make. You objected today, and since we have found some kind of a procedure where leading questions to some extent are not objected against, if you make an objection, would you please do it, whenever possible, as soon as the question has been asked. It has two advantages; first of all that the witness will not start answering, which saves time, and at the same time your objection is far more effective if the witness has not yet answered on the leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know. I was just trying to make sure that the witness didn't say something earlier in his answers that was then asked as a leading question. That could be a problem, and I do I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. So then we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
